piiFinding.summary: CONFIRMED live PII exposure on the Inspections tab's real (non-fixture) data path, predating this dispatch.
piiFinding.mechanism: src/mygov-live.mjs mapRealInspectionRecord() (line ~193) maps row.comments verbatim from smartcity-os's live /api/platform/mygov/inspections feed onto record.comments, with a comment citing the real staff dashboard's own insp.comments block as precedent. web/app.js inspectionRow() (line ~1039) renders record.comments directly into a table cell via td(record.comments, "t-data") -- an undocumented 'Comments' column not in any spec.
piiFinding.exampleTextClass: The dispatch's own PII examples (citizen names + phone numbers, e.g. 'DEBORAH MOORE, PH#737-762-6252') are exactly this class of field on this vendor.
piiFinding.accessGateVerified: Checked at source (src/tenancy.mjs): bastrop_tx carries accessPolicy 'tenant-private'; packContentReadStatus requires callerIsPackSubject (caller.kind==='tenant' AND caller.tenant===cityKey, resolved via Hauska MCP /auth/whoami) for a tenant-private pack. A 'service' bearer (DASHBOARDS_API_KEY) does NOT satisfy callerIsPackSubject. So this is NOT anonymous-reachable and NOT reachable by the shared service key -- the hard rule ('none of this data may reach ... any unauthenticated surface') is not violated. It IS reachable by any authenticated Bastrop tenant caller, which is still a live violation of the PII rule's actual requirement ('the free-text description is not a list column on any tab').
relatedLatentPaths: src/mygov-live.mjs mapRealCodeViolationRecord(): subject: row.type || row.description || 'Untitled violation' -- falls back to the free-text description field when type is absent. Currently INERT because web/app.js codeViolationRow() reads record.violationType (which the real mapper never sets, only fixture generators do), not record.subject -- masked by an unrelated field-name mismatch bug, not by design.

src/mygov-permits.mjs (line ~60, pre-existing, not part of G-92/G-97): subject: row.title || row.description || row.type || 'Untitled permit' -- same fallback shape, and this one IS live: web/app.js renderPipeline() renders record.subject directly (td(record.subject, "subj")). Whether any real permit row actually lacks a title (making this reachable in practice) could not be verified without a live read, which is out of reach against G-122's open incident.
piiFinding.planned: Fix within this lane's own scope, since it is a strict subset of the column-spec rebuild: (1) Inspections table drops the Comments column entirely (matches approved spec exactly: Inspection # / Type / Address / Inspector / Result / Scheduled -- no description field). (2) Remove the '|| row.description' fallback from both mapRealCodeViolationRecord's and mapRealPermitRecord's subject construction so the free-text field can never reach a displayed field via that path, closing the latent one at the source rather than only at the renderer. (3) Will NOT strip record.comments from the wire (API JSON) -- the design README is explicit that the design decision is scoped to rendering ('not a list column'), not a data-layer gate, and building that gate is named as separate, future work. Will state this residual explicitly in the close: comments still transits the /api/domains/inspections JSON response for an authenticated tenant caller, inspectable via browser network tools even though nothing paints it.

Promote per-tab record counts onto the tab strip itself (inline, next to each tab label), sourced from the same domain map /api/city-domains already serves.

Demote the existing 4-tile .metrics strip per tab to the compact/secondary tier already closest to spec; expand each to the full metric list the mission names per tab (e.g. Pipeline gains requested/pending-docs/on-hold beyond the current 4).

Rewrite each tab's <table class="dt"> column set to the approved spec exactly, dropping every undocumented real-feed-only column (fees itemization stays -- money is not the PII class named here -- but description/comments does not).
Build ONE load component (inspector/manager/officer) replacing the ad hoc register calls, parameterized by roster + counting rule.
Add pagination (previous / position / total) at the foot of every table.

Add the List/Map/Performance segmented control on Work orders; Map renders an honest not-built state (the mapping component itself is G-121/G-124's pinned, held work -- building real mapping here would be scope creep into a HELD row) with its own basis; Performance absorbs the existing SLA summary + daily queue panels.

Run npm test in full before opening a PR.
